Linux sandbox setup, UID/GID switching, namespace isolation, Landlock, seccomp, and PID/TID helpers.

# Purpose
This file implements the Linux sandbox setup used by Firedancer. It provides the internal steps needed to isolate a process before normal work begins: clear environment variables, verify that only the expected file descriptors are open, switch user and group IDs, create and configure user and mount namespaces, write UID and GID maps, restrict namespaces, pivot the root file system, apply Landlock rules, set resource limits, drop capabilities, and enable `no_new_privs`. It also includes a seccomp filter entry point that installs a BPF filter after the rest of the sandbox is in place.

The file also contains helper functions that support sandbox policy checks and process state control. These helpers read kernel settings such as `cap_last_cap` and `unprivileged_userns_clone`, detect whether user namespaces need `CAP_SYS_ADMIN`, clear the process environment with `explicit_bzero`, and return the current process ID and thread ID from `/proc`. The public entry points [`fd_sandbox_enter`](<#fd_sandbox_enter>) and [`fd_sandbox_switch_uid_gid`](<#fd_sandbox_switch_uid_gid>) expose the main sandbox and credential-switching behavior to other code, while the remaining functions are private support routines for the sandbox implementation.
